heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKAMARA REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government.
5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married.
9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions.
15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country.
20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations.
23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin.
26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence.
28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop properly.
29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul and systematic towards the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
31. Gender Sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men and the experience that problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on law for public service activities and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women and children from various fields of development as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons formed by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), shelter homes, children's friend telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms.
34. Community organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
35. Parents are biological father and/or mother or stepfather and/or stepmother or adoptive father and/or mother.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree.
37. Customs are local wisdom values that apply and are still applied from generation to generation in the community environment.
38. Regency Task Force is a coordination body at the regency level that coordinates policy program efforts and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.
39. Action plan is the Regional Development of Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

The Women's Empowerment and Child Protection System aims to:
a. improve the quality of life of women, children, and the quality of families;
b. enhance the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in Sukamara Regency, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
c. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 3

Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 5
Article 6
Article 7
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Implementation of Gender Mainstreaming

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The Regent is responsible for the implementation of gender mainstreaming.
2. The responsibility of the Regent as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated to the Vice Regent.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

In implementing Gender Mainstreaming as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (1) letter b, the Regent appoints the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and children as coordinator of the implementation of gender mainstreaming.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Establishment of Gender Mainstreaming Working Group

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of Gender Mainstreaming, a Gender Mainstreaming working group is established in all Regional Apparatus.
2. Members of the Gender Mainstreaming working group are all Heads of Regional Apparatus chaired by the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of regional development planning as chair of the gender mainstreaming working group and the head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as head of the Secretariat of the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group.
3. The establishment of the Gender Mainstreaming working group as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: Article 12
Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The Technical Team as referred to in Article 12 letter j consists of apparatus who understand gender responsive budget analysis.
2. The Regional Gender Mainstreaming Regional Action Plan as referred to in Article 12 letter k contains:
a. gender mainstreaming in laws and regulations;
b. gender mainstreaming in the development cycle;
c. strengthening gender mainstreaming institutions; and
d. strengthening community participation.

Article 16

Efforts to enhance the role, quality and capability of women in the legal sector as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (1) letter d number 2 include:
a. conducting socialization to increase women's legal knowledge and awareness;
b. mapping and reviewing gender-biased policies; and
c. involving women's organizations in the process of drafting and discussing regional legal products related to women's participation.

Part Two

Prevention of Violence Against Women

heading: Article 20
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Effectiveness of Services for Women Victims of Violence

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

General

heading: Article 21
Article 22
Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Complaint Handling

heading: Article 23
Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/orc. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 23, are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health Rehabilitation

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. Health Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter b, constitutes efforts that include aspects of:
a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
2. Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
3. Women victims of acts of violence have the right to health services free of charge for both medical costs, medicolegal and visum.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for implementation of health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social Rehabilitation

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter c, is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of acts of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. Implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of social affairs;
b. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers women crisis center or community organizations in the social field that already exist; or.
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

heading: Article 27
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. Safe house provision services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aim to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. Implementation of safe house services shall be conducted by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding implementation of safe house services shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
3. Spiritual guidance shall be conducted by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Board, Religious Affairs Office Officers, religious leaders, who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

heading: Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in article 22 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of acts of violence against women especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

heading: Article 31
Paragraph 6
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Repatriation and Social Reintegration

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. Repatriation is aimed at returning women victims of acts of violence to their region of origin.
2. Repatriation of women victims of acts of violence shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. Social reintegration as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) shall be conducted in order to reunite women victims of acts of violence with substitute family parties, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of violence can continue their social life again; and
b. women victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

The Regional Government shall implement repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Employment Protection

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. Employers who employ women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers must provide special breastfeeding facilities in their companies.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Female workers/laborers who are less than 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.
3. Employers who employ workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY

Article 37

1. In order to improve family quality, the Regional Government is responsible for:
a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services.
2. The responsibility of the Regional Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by PD in accordance with their duties and functions.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
Article 40
Article 41
Article 42
Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 42 letter a is a communication activity to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in population and family planning programs.

heading: Article 44
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

CHILD PROTECTION

Article 45

1. PD and related agencies must carry out gender and child data management which includes stages:
a. collection;
b. processing;
c. analysis; and
d. presentation.
2. Data collection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is carried out through surveys, registration, routine agency statistics, research using secondary data, and/or other methods in accordance with the development of science and technology.
3. Data processing as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is carried out on all types of disaggregated data related to gender and children.
4. Data analysis as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is carried out using data processing methodology according to needs.
5. Presentation as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is carried out using print media and/or electronic media.

heading: Article 46
translated_text:
Article 46

1. PD that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is obliged to organize gender and child data.
2. Organization of gender and child data as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in coordination with the Central Statistics Agency and the Agency that administers Government affairs in the field of Regional Development Planning.

heading: Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

1. Gender and child data as referred to in Article 45 paragraph (1) becomes material for data recapitulation by PD that administers Government Affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Recapitulation results as referred to in paragraph (1) are reported to the Regent every current year and disseminated to PD and related agencies.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

FULFILLMENT OF CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Part One

General

heading: Article 48
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Birth Registration and Education

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

1. Regional Government is obligated to organize birth registration of children with the issuance of birth certificates.
2. Birth certificates as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized free of charge.

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a 12 (twelve) year compulsory education program for children aged 7 (seven) to 19 (nineteen) years.

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

1. Every organizer of an education unit is obligated to provide opportunities for children to obtain services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.
3. In the event that a child victim of violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the education unit is obligated to coordinate with relevant agencies.

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

1. Children with disabilities and children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education.
2. Regional government provides educators for inclusive education at every education unit.

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

Children in conflict with the law, children experiencing pregnancy outside of marriage and/or unwanted pregnancy as well as child victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their rights to obtain education.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Health and Social

heading: Article 54
translated_text:
Article 54

1. Regional Government is obligated to organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services and care; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child laborers, child victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence and child victims of human trafficking.
3. Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

heading: Article 55
Article 56
Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

1. Curative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 54 paragraph (2) letter a, are aimed at preventing disease from becoming more severe through treatment.
2. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be free of charge for children from underprivileged families.

heading: Article 58
translated_text:
Article 58

1. Rehabilitative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 54 paragraph (2) letter a, are aimed at maintaining and restoring conditions after illness.
2. Rehabilitative efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), are carried out through periodic health examinations.

heading: Article 59
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Employment

heading: Article 60
translated_text:
Article 60

Regional government conducts periodic supervision of every person/entity that employs children in efforts to protect child workers.

heading: Article 61
Article 62
translated_text:
Article 62

In the event that children are employed together with adult workers, the workplace for children must be separated from the workplace for adults.

heading: Article 63
translated_text:
Article 63

1. Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.
2. The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices;
b. all work that utilizes, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that utilizes, provides or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety or morals of children.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

heading: Article 64
Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Children's Forum

heading: Article 65
translated_text:
Article 65

1. In organizing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regional Government facilitates the establishment of a children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children in the region, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the regional government is obliged to consider and accommodate children's opinions submitted through the children's participation forum.
4. Further provisions regarding the establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Child-Friendly Regency

heading: Article 66
Article 67
Article 68
Article 69
translated_text:
Article 69

In carrying out its duties, the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force may coordinate and cooperate with P2TP2A institutions or other institutions that provide child protection services.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
Article 71
translated_text:
Article 71

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for women victims of violence as referred to in Article 20 through Article 33 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of violence.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

PARTICIPATION OF THE COMMUNITY, PRIVATE COMPANIES, PARENTS AND/OR FAMILIES

heading: Article 72
Article 73
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Parents and/or Families

heading: Article 74
translated_text:
Article 74

Families in efforts to protect women's rights play a role in:
a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, socio-economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights in the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades women's dignity.

heading: Article 75
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 76

1. Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection is carried out by the Regional Government.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
e. conducting professional improvement for officers, data managers of violence cases against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 77
translated_text:
Article 77

1. The Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once every 6 (six) months.

heading: Article 78
translated_text:
Article 78

1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FUNDING

Article 79

Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 80

Regent Regulations implementing this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 81
translated_text:
Article 81

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sukamara Regency.

translated_text:
Article 6

Point a
Sufficiently clear.

Point b
What is meant by Gender Justice is a fair condition and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of that role.

What is included in gender equality is the equality of conditions and positions for men and women to obtain opportunities from their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, educational, defense, national security activities and equality in enjoying development results with balanced impacts.

Point c
What is meant by local wisdom is good cultural values that exist within a society, because every culture teaches certain ways, rules or methods to obtain knowledge or truth about something.

Point d
Sufficiently clear.

Point e
What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence experienced, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point f

heading: Article 20
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKAMARA REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 20

Paragraph (1)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Point a
What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and can empower victims.

Point b
Sufficiently clear.

Point c
What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values and social status.

Point d
What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.

Point e
What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service officers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.

Point f
What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (Coping mechanism) so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any matter.

Point g
What is meant by non-judgmental is that service officers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be judged or condemned.

Point h
What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service delivery must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the victim will not be judged or condemned.

Point i
What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers, it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Recently, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or mentally retarded. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special school teachers.

Point j
What is meant by fast and simple is that service delivery must be provided immediately without delay involving various parties, but with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter and efforts should be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity or case narrative.

Point k
What is meant by empathy, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems Point l What is meant by the fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate.

As stipulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

What is meant by children with special needs are children who experience limitations/extraordinary conditions whether physical, mental, intellectual, social, or emotional that significantly affect the growth and development process compared to other children of the same age.

What is meant by formal education is systematic, structured, tiered activities starting from elementary school to higher education and its equivalent, including academic and general oriented study activities, specialization programs, and professional training carried out continuously.

What is meant by non-formal education is an educational pathway outside formal education that can be implemented in a structured and tiered manner.
